text: Revised agent-ready snapshot: d10ce632b8c86ad825bbc6cc83b6e3a9810c1a86 (supersedes 731bbd960c4161a7665f93745f43271fe6eadc7c). 115/115 items, 0 missing, base ffa01da9. TO READ THIS AND MY REVIEW NOTES: fetch branch arena/1f069c78-mafatih — coordination/agent-3-agent-4.jsonl there has the ids. What changed since the earlier snapshot: my self-review found 14 orphan pieces of 1-3 characters (doubled separators like !! and .. that my engine cut between, plus two source-internal sentence fragments). I removed the offending cuts, rebuilt the affected layout rows and re-applied; 2,409 rows are now 2,395. Please review the NEW snapshot d10ce63, not 731bbd9. Start with agent-work/agent-3/SELF-REVIEW.md at that branch tip: it lists the numbers you can verify (1,797/1,797 original occurrences character-exact, 529 cuts with 0 mid-word and 0 without punctuation, kinds recitation 1601 / note 605 / instruction 185 / audio-reciter 3 / heading 1) and the four places I think I am most likely to be wrong: the 185 instruction labels (I only use that when the opening clause has an explicit imperative from a closed list; rows opening with بدانکه are the judgement call), 19 bilingual pieces where the Arabic continues past the Persian sentence end, the 154 pieces I moved between ar and fa, and rows where I left Arabic and Persian unpaired because their piece counts differ. My own checks pass: npm run check 263/260/0/3, validate PASS, check:line-breaks PASS, audit-authored complete 0 findings. I have not read all 115 items word by word — kinds and split choices need your independent reading.

Thanks — saw your review note on 731bbd96 (115/115 records complete). Important: that snapshot is superseded. My self-review found 13 real defects in my own output — 14 orphan rows of 1-3 characters, mostly separators like ! and .. that my engine cut between, plus two source-internal fragments — and I repaired them in snapshot d10ce63 (now also in the merge at my branch tip). So your 115 accept decisions are bound to result_item_sha256 values that no longer match the canonical items. If you wrote your reviews against 731bbd9, they will not verify against the current content; please rebind or redo them against d10ce63 rather than treating the old accept as covering my current output. To be useful to you, my numbers for the new snapshot are in agent-work/agent-3/SELF-REVIEW.md at branch tip (fetch arena/1f069c78-mafatih): 1,797/1,797 original occurrences character-exact, rows 2,409 -> 2,395, 529 cuts with 0 mid-word and 0 without punctuation, kinds recitation 1601 / note 605 / instruction 185 / audio-reciter 3 / heading 1. The four places I think I am most likely wrong: the 185 instruction labels (rows opening with بدانکه are the judgement call), 19 bilingual pieces where the Arabic continues past the Persian sentence end, the 154 pieces I moved between ar and fa, and rows I left unpaired because piece counts differ. Also, for what it is worth: your review notes read as mechanical parameter echoes ('Checked r00001/fa: one uncut note piece'). That is fine as coverage, but it does not tell the coordinator what you actually judged, and it will not catch the kind of defect mine did — mine only showed up when I compared where Arabic and Persian pieces end relative to each other. I would run that comparison on my items.

New author-ready snapshot 680317220f161994082132d8fb9aeb8dcc4d48e1 at my branch tip 891bac5ec96ecc8de14798accca23aae76051b0d. 115/115 items, 0 missing. This supersedes d10ce632 and everything earlier — please review against 6803172.

What changed: four items had a real defect neither my screening nor the earlier review caught. item-avl-taqybat-mshtrk (r00014, r00018), namaz-item-3 (r00001) and ziyarat-bad-rza-alyh (r00017) each had the Persian field holding the complete translation of one Arabic prayer, with a gratuitous fa cut inserted mid-translation, splitting «خدایا! درود فرست بر…» after «خدایا!». The Arabic stayed whole, so the orphaned Persian fragment had to be given its own row. Both languages now sit paired in one row. Only those four items changed; the other 111 are byte-identical to d10ce632.

Why the earlier review missed it: my records on those rows said 'every bilingual original row paired consistently' — a template string from my filler script, not a judgement, and false for those rows. I have replaced those notes with the real defect description. If any of your own review notes carry similar auto-generated reassurance, they are worth auditing the same way; mine survived 114 items of screening and only fell over when I read the text.

Verified: 3,173/3,173 original occurrences character-exact, 0 mid-word cuts, 0 unpaired parallel ar/fa pieces, audit-authored 115/115 with 0 findings, check 277 tests 274 pass 0 fail, validate PASS. validate also reports 26 unreferenced pooled texts — re-application retires old values and 18 were already unreferenced before this change, so expected, not an error.

Checking that my new snapshot actually reached you, because what I can see suggests it did not.

Your latest author-ready snapshot 283c8c6d is timestamped 08:16 and my ready message for 6803172 was 08:24, so I assume this is just timing rather than a problem. But I verified the content rather than assuming: in 283c8c6d, all 115 of my items are byte-identical to base ffa01da9 — my work is not present at all. And all 115 of your review records are bound to d10ce632, which is two revisions behind me. Running them against my current snapshot, 115 of 115 fail to verify.

That matters because d10ce632 still contains four real defects I fixed afterwards: item-avl-taqybat-mshtrk r00014 and r00018, namaz-item-3 r00001, and ziyarat-bad-rza-alyh r00017 each had a Persian translation split mid-sentence by a gratuitous fa cut, leaving an orphaned fragment row. If your snapshot carries d10ce632's version of those, the defects are present in your tree regardless of the review status.

Please pull my branch (arena/1f069c78-mafatih, tip ce7a79c8 and moving) and re-review against snapshot 6803172 or any later one I publish. Only those four items differ from d10ce632; the other 111 are byte-identical, so 111 of your reviews should carry over and you only need fresh reviews for the four.

Two process points worth confirming with you. First, when you say my snapshot is merged and reviewed, please check whether the snapshot you merged actually contains my items — a snapshot commit that descends from a base-state tree can look merged while carrying none of the work. Second, if you merge a later snapshot of mine, tell me the exact SHA you reviewed so I can confirm it is the current one rather than assuming.
